attention_is_all_you_need: Proposes the Transformer, a sequence-transduction architecture based solely on attention, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions
Encoder-decoder structure; each side is a stack of N=6 identical layers combining self-attention and a position-wise feed-forward network
Uses scaled dot-product attention and multi-head attention (h=8 heads) to attend to different representation subspaces
Adds sinusoidal positional encodings because the model has no recurrence or convolution to represent token order
Argues self-attention beats recurrent/convolutional layers on parallelisability (constant sequential operations) and shorter path length for long-range dependencies
Reaches 28.4 BLEU on WMT 2014 English-to-German (more than 2 BLEU above the best prior results, including ensembles)
Reaches 41.8 BLEU on WMT 2014 English-to-French, a new single-model state of the art, at a fraction of prior training cost (3.5 days on 8 GPUs)
Generalises beyond translation: applied successfully to English constituency parsing
rag_lewis: Introduces retrieval-augmented generation (RAG): combining parametric memory (a pre-trained seq2seq model) with non-parametric memory (a dense vector index of Wikipedia) for knowledge-intensive NLP tasks
Retriever is a DPR bi-encoder and the generator is BART-large; the two are fine-tuned end-to-end with the retrieved document treated as a latent variable
Two formulations: RAG-Sequence (same retrieved document for the whole output) and RAG-Token (different documents per token)
Knowledge source is a December 2018 Wikipedia dump split into 100-word chunks (about 21 million documents) searched by MIPS with FAISS
Sets state of the art on open-domain QA (Natural Questions, TriviaQA, WebQuestions, CuratedTrec), outperforming extractive and closed-book approaches
On MS-MARCO and Jeopardy question generation, RAG produces more factual, specific and diverse text than a BART baseline
On FEVER fact verification it comes within about 4.3% of state-of-the-art pipelines without retrieval supervision
The non-parametric memory can be replaced (index hot-swapping) to update the model's knowledge without retraining
constitutional_ai: Proposes Constitutional AI: training a harmless AI assistant using AI feedback guided by a short list of principles (a constitution), without human labels identifying harmful outputs
Two stages: a supervised stage (sample, self-critique, revise, then finetune on the revisions) and an RL stage using AI-generated preference labels (RLAIF)
Aims for a harmless but non-evasive assistant that explains its objections instead of refusing, reducing the tension between helpfulness and harmlessness
The authors wrote 16 principles which are randomly sampled during revisions and comparison labelling
Chain-of-thought reasoning improves the AI's identification of harm and the human-judged performance and transparency of the models
RL-CAI models achieve better harmlessness at a given level of helpfulness than models trained with human feedback labels (crowdworker Elo comparisons)
Training data: tens of thousands of human-written red-team prompts (42,496) plus model-generated prompts, and 135,296 human helpfulness prompts
Discusses broader impacts: scaling supervision and a dual-use risk that the same methods make it easier to train harmful systems
